stories.headline: Accenture spends $4.18B on Dragos majority stake plus runZero and NetRise to push into OT security

key_facts.fact: Accenture announced Thursday it will take a majority stake in Dragos and fully acquire runZero and NetRise at a combined enterprise value of approximately $4.175 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Accenture has entered into agreements to acquire a majority stake in Dragos and 100% of runZero and NetRise at a combined enterprise value of approximately $4.175 billion

key_facts.fact: The Dragos majority stake is valued at $3.25 billion; the deal builds on Accenture's existing $10 billion cybersecurity business and the targets together generate $208 million in annual recurring revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Accenture announced Thursday it would acquire a majority stake in industrial cybersecurity firm Dragos for $3.25 billion and purchase two smaller security companies outright, essentially making a $4.18 billion bet

key_facts.fact: Dragos is an OT threat-detection specialist; runZero (founded by Metasploit creator HD Moore) handles asset discovery and attack-surface intelligence; NetRise focuses on firmware-level visibility and software supply chain security.
key_facts.excerpt: NetRise contributes deep firmware analysis and software supply chain visibility capabilities, while runZero, the company founded by renowned cybersecurity expert and Metasploit creator HD Moore, adds advanced asset discovery, exposure assessment, and attack surface intelligence.

key_facts.fact: The transactions are expected to close in August or September 2026; Dragos CEO Robert M. Lee will continue leading the combined business.
key_facts.excerpt: The transactions are expected to close in August or September 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approvals.

key_facts.fact: Accenture shares fell over 11% in premarket trading as the company cut its FY revenue growth forecast top end to 3–4% (from 3–5%), signaling weak discretionary IT consulting spend.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Accenture fell over 11 per cent in premarket trading as the company cut the top end of its annual revenue growth forecast range, signalling businesses wary of an uncertain economy are curtailing spending on discretionary IT consulting projects.

stories.headline: Amazon in talks to sell Trainium AI chips for use in third-party data centers

key_facts.fact: Amazon's senior vice president overseeing semiconductor, AI and quantum, Peter DeSantis, said AWS is in talks to sell its Trainium AI chips for use in other companies' data centers — chips previously exclusive to AWS.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's AI chief Peter DeSantis told Bloomberg that AWS is in talks to sell its AI chip Trainium to other companies for use in data centers.

key_facts.fact: DeSantis said a key driver is rising international demand — particularly in Europe — for locally controlled, sovereign AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: a major driver behind the push is rising international demand for locally controlled computing resources — particularly in Europe, where regulatory and political pressure has increased calls for sovereign AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: DeSantis dismissed concerns the external sales would cannibalize AWS cloud revenue, citing 'so much underconsumption in AI.'
key_facts.excerpt: "There's so much underconsumption in AI. I'm not worried about it," he said.

key_facts.fact: CEO Andy Jassy estimated in April that selling Amazon's chips at run-rate to AWS and outside customers could push the chip business toward ~$50B in annualized revenue, up from a current ~$20B run rate across Trainium, Graviton and Nitro.
key_facts.excerpt: putting the company's annualized chip revenue at roughly $20 billion across the Trainium, Graviton, and Nitro product lines. Jassy wrote at the time that selling to both AWS and external customers could push that figure toward $50 billion annually.

key_facts.fact: Trainium-line revenue commitments exceed $225 billion as of April, and Trainium4 is already booked more than a year ahead of shipment.
key_facts.excerpt: Trainium sold out almost right away, and Trainium4 is already booked more than a year before launch.

key_facts.fact: The move mirrors a similar shift by Google, which has begun selling its custom TPUs to select external data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: The approach follows a similar path taken by Google, which recently announced plans to sell its custom chips to select external data centers.

stories.headline: Apple opens iOS to alternative app marketplaces and external payments in Brazil under CADE deal

key_facts.fact: Apple announced on June 18 that iOS developers in Brazil can distribute apps through alternative marketplaces and process payments outside Apple's In-App Purchase, as part of a settlement with Brazilian competition regulator CADE.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple today announced changes impacting iOS apps in Brazil that reflect a recent agreement with Brazil's competition regulator, the Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (CADE). These updates create new options for developers to distribute apps on alternative app marketplaces and to process app payments for digital goods and services outside of Apple In-App Purchase.

key_facts.fact: Apps distributed outside the App Store will pay a 5% Core Technology Commission on digital goods and services; alternative marketplaces must be authorized by Apple.
key_facts.excerpt: Core Technology Commission: iOS apps distributed outside of the App Store in Brazil will pay a 5 percent commission on the sale of digital goods and services, including paid apps.

key_facts.fact: Inside the App Store, the standard commission on digital goods drops to a maximum of 21% (from up to 30%), with a reduced 10% rate for Small Business Program, Video Partner Program, and subscriptions after their first year; in-app purchase adds a 5% processing fee.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the new terms, developers who distribute their apps through the App Store and use Apple's IAP system will be subject to a 5% payment processing fee, plus a 21% App Store commission. That commission drops to 10% for developers enrolled in programs such as the App Store Small Business Program, Video Partner Program, and Mini Apps Partner Program

key_facts.fact: Developers who direct users to an external website will pay a 15% Store Services Commission for purchases completed within seven days of an external purchase link tap.
key_facts.excerpt: Developers who distribute their apps through the App Store and direct users to an external payment provider will pay a 15% Store Services Commission.

key_facts.fact: The changes ship on iOS 26.5 and later; current Apple Developer Program members must agree to the updated license terms by July 6, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: These changes are available on iOS 26.5 and later, and they are the result of regulatory action from Brazil's competition regulator.

key_facts.fact: The CADE dispute originated from a 2022 complaint by Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre.
key_facts.excerpt: Late last year, Apple reached an agreement with Brazil's competition watchdog, CADE, resolving a dispute that began in 2022 after Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre filed a complaint over the company's App Store rules.

stories.headline: US Commerce Sec Lutnick tells ASML he suspects a top EUV chip tool may have reached China

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told ASML senior leaders in a series of recent meetings that he's concerned one of the Dutch company's EUV lithography machines may have made it into China in violation of US-led export restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: In a series of recent meetings, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick outlined concerns to ASML's senior leaders that one of its top-of-the-line machines may have made its way into China, in violation of US-led export restrictions.

key_facts.fact: ASML has never been allowed to ship EUV systems to China due to curbs imposed under the first Trump administration; EUV machines are required by TSMC to manufacture processors for Nvidia and Apple.
key_facts.excerpt: EUV systems are used by firms such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to manufacture processors for the likes of Nvidia and Apple, and ASML has never been allowed to ship them to China

key_facts.fact: ASML created and circulated a document in Washington titled 'No indication of any ASML EUV System in China' after the April meeting with Lutnick; it states there are 314 EUV machines in operation worldwide, 26 decommissioned, and none in China.
key_facts.excerpt: There are 314 EUV machines in operation around the world, 26 that have been decommissioned, and none in China, according to the document

key_facts.fact: Senior administration officials told Bloomberg they have evidence ASML shipped specialty equipment used to transport EUV machines as well as other components, but said the proof is too sensitive to disclose.
key_facts.excerpt: The senior administration officials said that they have evidence of ASML shipping to China specialty equipment used to transport EUV machines, as well as other components that could be used in EUV systems. The proof of those exports is too sensitive to disclose

key_facts.fact: A bipartisan bill moving through Congress would go further and ban all of ASML's deep ultraviolet (DUV) shipments to China; DUV accounts for roughly 20% of ASML's expected 2026 revenue. The bill cleared a key committee in April.
key_facts.excerpt: a bipartisan bill moving through Congress would go much further than EUV — it calls for an effective ban on all of ASML's deep ultraviolet (DUV) shipments to China, the less advanced lithography tools that account for roughly a fifth of the company's expected 2026 revenue.

key_facts.fact: ASML says EUV machines are the size of a school bus, weigh 180 tons, and that customers 'cannot remove, transport and relocate EUV systems without ASML involvement due to specialised handling procedures.'
key_facts.excerpt: ASML's most advanced EUV systems are roughly the size of a school bus and weigh 180 tons. 'ASML has never shipped an EUV machine to China nor have we shipped to China any component, module or equipment specially designed to be used in an EUV machine'

stories.headline: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick tells ASML one of its EUV machines may be in China; ASML denies

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told ASML's senior leaders in a series of recent meetings that one of its top-of-the-line EUV lithography machines may have made its way into China in violation of US-led export restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: In a series of recent meetings, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick outlined concerns to ASML's senior leaders that one of its top-of-the-line machines may have made its way into China, in violation of US-led export restrictions.

key_facts.fact: ASML has never been allowed to ship EUV systems to China because of curbs imposed during the first Trump administration; EUV is used by TSMC to manufacture processors for Nvidia and Apple.
key_facts.excerpt: EUV systems are used by firms such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to manufacture processors for the likes of Nvidia Corp. and Apple Inc., and ASML has never been allowed to ship them to China because of curbs imposed during the first Trump administration.

key_facts.fact: ASML denies the claim, saying the tools are the size of a school bus, manufactured in limited quantities, and require constant upkeep from ASML employees — and that no EUV machine is in China.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML has pushed back on Lutnick's suggestion, explaining that none of these tools — which are the size of a school bus, are manufactured in limited quantities, and require constant upkeep from ASML employees — are in China.

key_facts.fact: Senior US officials say they have evidence ASML shipped EUV-related components and transport equipment to China but have repeatedly declined to share it with Bloomberg or ASML; ASML circulated a document in Washington in April titled 'No indication of any ASML EUV System in China'.
key_facts.excerpt: Senior administration officials told Bloomberg they have evidence that ASML shipped EUV-related components and transport equipment to China, though they've declined, repeatedly, to show it — to Bloomberg or, apparently, to ASML itself.

key_facts.fact: A bipartisan US bill (MATCH Act) introduced in April 2026 would ban all ASML DUV shipments to China, going beyond the existing EUV ban; DUV currently accounts for roughly a fifth of ASML's expected 2026 revenue, and China's share of system sales fell from 36% to 19% in Q1 2026 due to stricter controls.
key_facts.excerpt: In April 2026, U.S. lawmakers introduced the MATCH Act, a bill that would also ban the export of DUV immersion machines and the servicing of existing machines in China. China recently accounted for 36 percent of system sales, but that share dropped to 19 percent in the first quarter of 2026 due to stricter controls.

stories.headline: Ex-White House AI adviser Dean Ball joins OpenAI to lead new Strategic Futures team

key_facts.fact: Dean Ball, former Senior Policy Adviser for AI and Emerging Technology in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, will join OpenAI on July 6 as head of a new team called Strategic Futures.
key_facts.excerpt: our colleague Dean W. Ball is joining OpenAI as Head of Strategic Futures on July 6.

key_facts.fact: Strategic Futures will report to Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon and span both public-facing policy proposals and OpenAI's internal governance, working with the Preparedness, legal, policy, National Security and Global Affairs teams.
key_facts.excerpt: its work will cover both public-facing policy (for example, proposals for legislation) and internal governance within the lab, working in close collaboration with members of the technical staff, the Preparedness team, the legal team, policy staff from the National Security and Global Affairs teams

key_facts.fact: The team's mandate explicitly covers catastrophic risk, recursive self-improvement, labor market impact and the relationship between frontier labs and government.
key_facts.excerpt: charged with shaping frontier AI policy, which is to say matters pertaining to: catastrophic risk, recursive self-improvement, labor market impact, and the relationship between the frontier labs, governments (particularly the U.S. Federal Government), and society.

key_facts.fact: Ball co-authored the White House AI Action Plan released last summer and previously was a senior fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation — a role he will retain on a non-resident basis.
key_facts.excerpt: Few people have shaped AI policy as directly as Dean, from his writing at Hyperdimensional, to his co-authorship of the White House AI Action Plan … Happily, Dean will stay on with FAI as a non-resident senior fellow

key_facts.fact: Ball has publicly criticized the Trump administration's actions against Anthropic, including the Pentagon's designation of the company as a supply-chain risk and the White House's export limits on Anthropic's Fable model.
key_facts.excerpt: Ball has also previously criticized the Trump administration's dispute with Anthropic, including the Pentagon's designation of the company as a … chain risk and the White House's export limits on Anthropic's Fable AI model

key_facts.fact: The hire follows OpenAI's recent recruitment of Noam Shazeer from Google to lead architecture research.
key_facts.excerpt: His appointment follows closely on the heels of the company successfully recruiting AI expert Noam Shazeer from Google.

key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition, the New York-based startup building a foundation model that trains AI agents how to move through space and time, is in talks to raise around $300 million … The fresh funds would bring the startup's valuation up to just over $2 billion

key_facts.fact: Backers in the new round include Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt, plus existing investors Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst.

key_facts.excerpt: GLM-5.2 is the leading open weights model on the Intelligence Index v4.1. At 51, it leads MiniMax-M3 (44), DeepSeek V4 Pro (max, 44) and Kimi K2.6 (43).

key_facts.fact: Among frontier models overall, GLM-5.2 (51) trails only Fable 5 (60), Opus 4.8 (56) and GPT-5.5 (55) on the index — placing it on the Pareto frontier of intelligence vs cost per task.

key_facts.fact: The model retains the GLM-5.1 architecture footprint at 744B total parameters with 40B active per inference, but expands the context window from 200K to 1M tokens.

key_facts.fact: Capability gains concentrate in scientific reasoning: CritPt +16 points to 21%, Humanity's Last Exam +12 points to 40%, SciCode +7 points to 50%; GDPval-AA v2 reaches 1524 versus 1514 for proprietary GPT-5.5.

stories.headline: Google guarantees $3.2B to fund NY data center that will rent its TPUs to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Google provided a $3.2 billion financial guarantee to fund a New York data center that will rent its tensor processing units (TPUs) to Anthropic, mirroring Nvidia's playbook of underwriting customer demand for its chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Google provided a $3.2 billion financial guarantee for the project to boost its AI chip game and challenge NVIDIA's lead. The company is backing Anthropic by powering its work with Google's own TPUs (tensor processing units) at a huge New York data center, pretty much mirroring how NVIDIA encourages demand for its GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Google plans to sell TPUs more directly to outside customers and has rolled out a new chip; some clients are seeing up to 30% cost savings and 4x performance versus alternatives, with Google planning to raise $85 billion for more AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Google isn't stopping there: it's now planning to sell TPUs directly to more customers and has rolled out a new chip designed for faster, cheaper AI processing. Some clients are already seeing up to 30% cost savings and four times the speed. Plus, Google plans to raise $85 billion for even more AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic earlier disclosed an April 2026 deal with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity starting in 2027; Claude's run-rate revenue reached $30 billion in 2026, up from about $9 billion at end of 2025, with 1,000+ business customers each spending over $1 million annually.
key_facts.excerpt: We have signed a new agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity that we expect to come online starting in 2027. Our run-rate revenue has now surpassed $30 billion—up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025. Today that number exceeds 1,000, doubling in less than two months.

key_facts.fact: Google has previously contracted to sell three million TPUs to Intel for production beginning in 2028 and is in talks with Samsung for its next-gen 'Icefish' 10th-gen TPU and Axion processors, signaling a broader push to diversify foundry sourcing as it scales its custom-silicon business.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is discussing two separate Samsung engagements. One covers its next-generation Axion processors expected around 2028, while the other involves components tied to its 10th-generation Tensor Processing Unit, codenamed Icefish, which is being co-developed with MediaTek.

key_facts.fact: Lee will scale advanced packaging technologies into high-volume manufacturing, including EMIB-T (Intel's 2.5D packaging) and High-Density Hybrid Bonding (HBI), a next-generation 3D packaging process; Navid Shahriari, who had been responsible for packaging, will retire.

stories.headline: Samsung Foundry wins talks with AMD, Google, Tesla, Groq as TSMC capacity sells out

key_facts.fact: According to a Nikkei Asia report, a growing list of major chip customers — including AMD, Google, Nvidia-backed Groq, Tesla, and BYD — are in discussions with Samsung Foundry about manufacturing future chips as TSMC's leading-edge capacity is fully booked.
key_facts.excerpt: According to a report from Nikkei Asia, a growing list of major chip customers, including AMD, Google, Nvidia-backed Groq, Tesla, and BYD, are in discussions with Samsung Foundry about manufacturing future chips as demand continues to outstrip TSMC's available capacity.

key_facts.fact: AMD is in talks with Samsung to manufacture certain future CPUs starting in 2028 on Samsung's second-generation 2nm node — its first reported CPU shift to Samsung, with AMD's GPUs remaining at TSMC.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD is reportedly in talks with Samsung about manufacturing certain future CPUs starting in 2028.

key_facts.fact: Google is discussing two separate Samsung engagements: next-gen Axion processors around 2028 and components for its 10th-gen TPU codenamed 'Icefish', co-developed with MediaTek.

key_facts.fact: Tesla has confirmed its next-generation AI6 chip will be produced at Samsung's Texas facility; BYD is in talks with Samsung on 2nm and 4nm autonomous driving SoCs; Groq's LP30 AI inference processor will run on Samsung's 4nm node.

key_facts.fact: AMD stock rose ~3% and Intel ~4% on June 18 as investors reacted to the Samsung-AMD talks; the TSMC capacity squeeze is also driving overflow to Intel Foundry, with reports that Apple could use Intel's 18A-P process for future M7 production in 2027 and Google ordered 3 million TPUs from Intel for 2028.

stories.headline: Midjourney launches medical division and full-body ultrasound scanner, with no FDA clearance yet

key_facts.fact: Midjourney, the AI image generator, announced Midjourney Medical and 'The Midjourney Scanner' (its first hardware product) at a June 17, 2026 San Francisco event and a June 18 blog post; CEO David Holz. The full-body ultrasound scanner lowers a user into a shallow pool of water while a ring of sensors images the body with no radiation or magnets, which Holz claims is 'in many ways superior to even MRI machines' in about 60 seconds (vs 60-90 minutes for a full-body MRI).
key_facts.excerpt: Dubbed The Midjourney Scanner, it's an ultrasound-based full-body scanner that uses a ring of sensors to capture vertical slices of the inside of your body... it 'aims for image quality comparable to MRI in many ways.'

key_facts.fact: Reality check: the current prototype takes roughly 20 minutes per scan (not 60 seconds), has been used on about a dozen people, uses no AI in its imaging pipeline yet ('We're not even using any AI in this yet,' Holz said), and has no FDA clearance for diagnosis. Midjourney has never built or operated a regulated medical device.
key_facts.excerpt: the current prototype takes roughly 20 minutes per scan, has been used on about a dozen people, runs without any AI in its imaging pipeline, and carries no FDA clearance for diagnosing anything.

key_facts.fact: It goes to market as a wellness product producing 'detailed body composition maps' (which do not require FDA clearance under the general wellness policy); the company says it has begun FDA discussions and will submit regular test results to incrementally obtain clearance for diagnostic capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: We're starting by just giving you detailed body composition maps - and we'll be submitting regular test results to the FDA for increased capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The hardware was built with Butterfly Network, an ultrasound-on-chip maker Midjourney licensed exclusively in November 2025, using about 40 of its ultrasound-on-chip modules per machine; the project is led by Ahmad Abbas, a former hardware engineering manager on Apple's Vision Pro. The underlying technique, Ultrasound Computed Tomography (USCT), is not new and has been an active research project at Caltech.
key_facts.excerpt: the company is developing the machine with handheld ultrasound device maker Butterfly Network. Midjourney signed a licensing agreement with Butterfly Network in November 2025, securing exclusive rights to its ultrasound-on-chip technology. The project is led by Ahmad Abbas, Midjourney's head of consumer hardware projects, who joined the company in late 2023 after working on the Vision Pro at Apple.

key_facts.fact: Midjourney plans to debut the scanner inside a roughly 25,000 sq ft 'Midjourney Spa' near Union Square in San Francisco (with 9-10 scanners alongside hot tubs, saunas and cold plunges) around the end of 2027, and aims for a fleet of more than 50,000 scanners doing about 1 billion scans a month by 2031; it claims enough early imaging could one day 'avoid 30 percent of all deaths and 50 percent of all healthcare costs.' The scanner is one of eight Midjourney projects (four hardware, four software).
key_facts.excerpt: it wants a fleet of more than 50,000 scanners worldwide by 2031, with capacity for 'a billion scans a month', and claims that enough early imaging could one day 'avoid 30 per cent of all deaths and 50 per cent of all healthcare costs'.
